endorsements.quote: Such carriers may take the form of dedicated laboratories, formally chartered governance committees, or federated institutional arrangements, but must remain structurally distinct from temporary project teams and independent of short-term funding cycles.

Effective governance therefore requires that regulatory authorization and accountability structures be established prior to deployment, particularly in regulatory environments that continue to evolve alongside emerging clinical AI capabilities.
Governance fit refers to the calibrated alignment between governance intensity and system characteristics such as clinical risk, update frequency, and operational complexity [ 25 , 33 ].
Staged deployment strategies similarly enable systems to evolve within monitored operational environments before wider clinical integration [ 34 ].

A consistent governance principle nevertheless emerges, whereby sustained clinical deployment requires clearly defined roles, decision rights, and accountability structures linking algorithm development, clinical use, and institutional oversight.

unlisted_practices: Govern data pipelines, computational resources, and interoperability systems as durable institutional infrastructure under defined accountability, independent of project-bound funding cycles.
Establish governance pathways linking localized AI deployment with institution-wide authority structures to enable scaling.
Integrate patient and community involvement into lifecycle governance through defined feedback channels and transparent communication of system use boundaries.
Use risk-tiered update thresholds and predefined authorization pathways so low-risk model refinements proceed under simplified authorization while high-impact modifications receive stricter review.
